subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
title: Ductus Venosus, Foramen Ovale and Fetal Haemoglobin

steps.tx: The shunt carrying oxygenated umbilical vein blood past the liver into the inferior vena cava is the **ductus venosus**. It delivers the best oxygenated blood toward the heart and brain. After birth it fibroses into the ligamentum venosum. Roughly a fifth of umbilical vein blood takes this shunt, rising when the fetus is short of oxygen.
steps.say: The ductus venosus shunts oxygenated blood past the liver toward heart and brain.

steps.tx: The flap opening between the two atria directing blood right to left is the **foramen ovale**. It lets oxygenated blood bypass the lungs into the systemic circulation. Rising left atrial pressure at birth closes the flap functionally. The flap is the septum primum, pressed shut when left atrial pressure exceeds right at the first breaths.
steps.say: The foramen ovale directs oxygenated blood right to left, bypassing the fetal lungs.

steps.tx: The vessel joining pulmonary artery to aorta in fetal life is the **ductus arteriosus**. It diverts most right ventricular output away from fluid filled lungs. Prostaglandins keep it open before birth, and its closure follows birth. Indomethacin given to stop preterm labour can close it early, which is why fetal echocardiography monitors such treatment.
steps.say: The ductus arteriosus diverts right ventricular output away from the fluid filled lungs.

steps.tx: Fetal blood uses haemoglobin F with two gamma chains, giving **fetal haemoglobin** its properties. Higher oxygen affinity suits placental gas exchange. Raised levels persist in some inherited blood disorders in adults. Two alpha and two gamma chains make haemoglobin F, written alpha2 gamma2 in examinations.
steps.say: Fetal haemoglobin uses gamma chains and higher affinity for placental oxygen exchange.

steps.tx: At birth, clamping the cord and inflating the lungs trigger **circulatory transition**. Pulmonary resistance falls dramatically while systemic resistance rises. These pressure reversals close the fetal shunts over hours to days. Cord clamping raises systemic resistance at the same moment, so delaying clamping by a minute transfers extra blood to the baby.
steps.say: Circulatory transition at birth reverses pressures and closes the fetal shunts.

steps.tx: Failure of the ductus arteriosus to close after birth gives a **patent ductus arteriosus**. It is commoner in premature babies and causes heart failure from left to right shunting. Indomethacin or surgical ligation closes persistent ducts. A continuous murmur with bounding pulses in a preterm baby is the bedside picture, confirmed on echocardiography.
steps.say: A patent ductus in premature babies causes heart failure and may need drug closure.

steps.tx: Doppler study of the ductus venosus assesses fetal wellbeing in growth restriction, termed **ductus venosus Doppler**. Absent or reversed flow during atrial contraction signals decompensation. It times delivery in early severe growth restriction. Reversed a wave in the ductus venosus after 32 weeks often triggers delivery planning in early growth restriction.
steps.say: Ductus venosus Doppler signals decompensation in early severe fetal growth restriction.

steps.tx: Oxygenated blood streaming preferentially to the brain via the foramen ovale is called **preferential streaming**. Anatomy directs ductus venosus blood across the foramen to the left heart. The developing brain thus receives the richest blood available. Blood from the ductus venosus streams across the foramen while poorer blood from the lower body goes toward the lungs and ductus arteriosus.
steps.say: Preferential streaming delivers the richest blood to the developing fetal brain.

steps.tx: Persistence of fetal circulation with right to left shunting after birth causes **persistent pulmonary hypertension** of the newborn. Hypoxia maintains high pulmonary resistance and cyanosis despite oxygen. Inhaled nitric oxide is a key treatment. Treatment adds surfactant, gentle ventilation and inhaled nitric oxide, and severe cases may need extracorporeal support.
steps.say: Persistent pulmonary hypertension keeps fetal shunting after birth and needs nitric oxide.
